![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119854/assets/ec03c28e17138917d31898f165925cb246cf1f81a03f15672f87dde586b06ed2.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ is the path comprising of a horizontal line segment of length $2$ and a semicircle of radius $2,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=1.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1}=1-1=0.
$$
